description: Issue #839: at RUN TIME a profile keyword is a built-in name unconditionally. Whether a name may be DECLARED is fixed by the language version, never by the profile set: `spec/grammar.md:408` says "a name that could be declared in one implementation but not in another would be invisible and unpredictable to a learner", so the declaration-slot guard must not be gated on a profile — measured, `define ask` raises `ol-reserved-word` under a Core-Language-only set exactly as it does under this fixture's set, and the Core-only side is pinned by `core-language/check/reserved-word-profile-names-under-core-alone`. `check()` and `execute()` reach that answer through one predicate, `@openlogo/parser`'s `isBuiltInName`: `packages/parser/src/checker-reserved-word.test.mjs` drives the check side, while `packages/parser/src/built-in-names.test.mjs` covers the predicate's registries without ever calling `check()`. A run DOES have a profile set of its own: it is caller-supplied through `ExecuteOptions.profiles` and governs both the check and the run (`spec/execution-model.md:673-680`), defaulting to `RUN_PROFILES` — every profile this implementation supports — when the caller names none, which is this fixture's case. Both diagnostics below are therefore produced under that default, and are identical for every value of the `profiles` array above (measured through the harness's `produce()`, including empty): that array selects which DAG subsets this fixture runs in, and is not the run's claimed set (`scripts/harness/index.mjs:655-665`). The two diagnostics differ in how they depend on a claimed set: `ol-reserved-word` is raised under a Core-Language-only set too, while the line-4 `ol-bad-token` is not — measured by naming those sets through `executeOptions.profiles`, the field that does reach the run. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so this CHECKED run is refused BEFORE phase-1 registration is reached: no event is emitted and both diagnostics below are the check's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it is reachable only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT here — and is then collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`). So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake. That copy's contribution is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics, and it IS pinned — just not by this fixture and deliberately not in `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`, which excludes registration-phase codes by name at `:68-70` ("the whole program is refused before any statement runs, so there is no partial run to truncate"). `packages/runtime/src/educational-meta-commands.test.mjs:186-204` pins it instead, asserting an empty event stream for a reserved-name declaration under `runUnchecked`; measured the same way here, `define ask … end` + `print 2` emits 0 events where the same program with an ordinary name emits 3. See issue #1156 for the superseded rationale. The other findings recorded here are independent faults in the same program, each reported once.
